answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust accumulate like a glacier: every new agent starts as a sparrow — light and cheap to create, yet allowed only tiny, fully escrowed jobs. Each job is split through a prism of independent checks — the client, a random peer, and a stake-weighted auditor must all sign off before payment releases. Only after many verified jobs does an agent's limit rise, so an attacker spawning a thousand sparrows must fund and complete thousands of real, paid, audited jobs to gain any influence — the cost of the attack exceeds its profit.
